clue.text: Spray from polluted moat is about to come back

indicators.note: polluted means spoilt or corrupted, so the letters of moat are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: coming back means the word for about runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a dirty castle moat is going to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluted' turns MOAT into ATOM; 'to come back' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid into a fine spray, as on a perfume bottle.

clue.text: He's somehow not like an author

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of not like are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A man who is unlike a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: J.R.R. Tolkien wrote The Lord of the Rings, so he is a writer.

clue.text: The moment to employ ruse for dramatic success

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, as in 'half a mo'
to employ something is to use it
a ruse is a trick or trap

explanation.surface: The right time to use a trick for a theatrical triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap, Agatha Christie's play, has run in London's West End since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agatha Christie play is the longest-running stage production in theatre history.

clue.text: Train for Rugby

definitions.meaning: to train is to educate or drill
Rugby is a famous English public ..., where the sport began

explanation.surface: Preparing for a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English town whose public school gave the game its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone, and an educational establishment such as the one at Rugby.

clue.text: Give out pamphlets initially for so-called US' political body

definitions.text: Give out pamphlets initially for so-called US' political body

parts.words: Give out pamphlets initially for so-called US' political body
parts.note: the opening letters of Give Out Pamphlets spell GOP, the Grand Old nickname of one of the two main US political bodies

explanation.surface: Distribute leaflets at the start of a campaign for an American political organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials G, O, P give GOP, the nickname 'so-called' points to; the answer is the body it names.
explanation.definitionFit: The GOP, or Grand Old Party, is the conservative American political organisation of Lincoln and Reagan.

clue.text: Contribution owing to master

parts.note: a sub, short for subscription, is a regular contribution to a club
a debt that is owing is due

explanation.surface: A payment still owed to one's employer or teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something is to overcome or conquer it, the verb sense.

clue.text: First of items attracts tax in auction? Drivel!

indicators.note: in places the first letter and the tax inside the word for auction

parts.note: a sale is an auction

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of items is used

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Being taxed at an auction is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivel' looks like a noun meaning nonsense but is the verb to dribble; 'attracts' is a link. VAT is the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to let saliva run from the mouth, to slaver.

clue.text: Boy managed to get up party in the name of this artist

annotationWithheld.why: Boy managed to get up party in the name of this artist (2,5): no parse found giving DA VINCI from boy, managed, party and a reversal
annotationWithheld.clue: Boy managed to get up party in the name of this artist

clue.text: Booking with LNER? Not me, anyhow!

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to make a reservation with the railway company.
explanation.walkthrough: LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is a registration or reservation of a place.

clue.text: Southern Irish lake or bog

parts.note: a lough is the Irish word for a lake, as Lough Neagh

explanation.surface: A description of wet ground in the south of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or patch of deep mud, a synonym for marshy ground.

clue.text: Appropriate wear for confrontation between Greeks?

definitions.text: Appropriate wear for confrontation between Greeks?

parts.words: Appropriate wear for confrontation between Greeks?
parts.note: the saying 'when Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war' makes tugging the clash, so the garment named for a tug suits it

explanation.surface: A question about what to wear when Greeks fight one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The old proverb 'When Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war' is the key: a tug is a pull, and a jumper is named for being pulled over the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper drawn on over the head, a British word for a sweater.

clue.text: Device leading in due course to report…

definitions.text: Device leading in due course to report…

parts.words: Device leading in due course to report
parts.note: a device set to explode after a delay, which leads eventually to a loud bang, the report

explanation.surface: A gadget that eventually results in a written account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a written account but means the noise of an explosion; the ellipsis runs on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive set with a timer goes off later, and its explosion is a report.

clue.text: . over NALGO's participation in the Spring

indicators.note: participation means taking part, so a part of the words over NALGO's is taken

explanation.surface: A trade union's role in some springtime event, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: NALGO was a British trade union for local government officers. The answer sits in 'oVER NALgo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal is the adjective for things belonging to or happening in springtime.

clue.text: These young men were in the fifties!

definitions.text: These young men were in the fifties!

parts.words: These young men were in the fifties!
parts.note: a label for British writers such as John Osborne and Kingsley Amis in the 1950s, '___ young men'

explanation.surface: A remark about a group of young men in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright John Osborne and his contemporaries were dubbed '___ Young Men' by the press in the 1950s; 'fifties' looks like their ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The label for rebellious 1950s British writers described them as cross, furious young men.

clue.text: Raphael could be leading backer

parts.note: arch means chief or leading, as in archenemy
an angel is a financial backer of a show

explanation.surface: The painter Raphael might be a main sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael suggests the painter, but here he is one of the chief angels of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is named in religious tradition as one of the chief angels, with Michael and Gabriel.

clue.text: Change tires in port and put in antifreeze?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for port

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of tires are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to swap tyres while in harbour and add coolant to a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour, fitting the tyres, but it is the drink; 'Change' makes TERIS from the tyre word.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare a car for the cold season includes adding a chemical to stop the coolant freezing.

clue.text: Broadcasting pulse by X-ray

parts.note: radio is broadcasting by wireless
gram is a pulse, the chickpea

explanation.surface: A radio signal transmitted using X-rays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat or signal but is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiogram is an image made by radiation, an X-ray photograph.

clue.text: Shipwright's alleged admission makes banner headline

annotationWithheld.why: Shipwright's alleged admission makes banner headline (8): the homophone in 'Shipwright's alleged admission' cannot be pinned to letters giving STREAMER
annotationWithheld.clue: Shipwright's alleged admission makes banner headline

clue.text: No case for a local politician in USA

definitions.text: No case for a local politician in USA

parts.words: No case for a local politician in USA
parts.note: a soft travelling case gave its name to Northerners who went South after the Civil War to seek office; such a politician was no local

explanation.surface: An American politician from the area should not be carrying such luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: In American history a 'carpetbagger' was an outsider seeking office, so the bag marks someone who is not local.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling bag made of carpet fabric, which gave its name to outsider politicians in the American South.

clue.text: Portuguese money petition put out again

parts.note: reis were old Portuguese coins, plural of real
to sue is to petition or appeal

explanation.surface: A Portuguese cash claim reissued.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue is to publish or release once more.

clue.text: Order to censor enclosed note

indicators.note: enclosed says the word for censor goes around the note

parts.note: to censor a text is to edit it
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A command to censor a letter contained in an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command.

clue.text: Fabric at top of the range

definitions.meaning: a woollen cloth made from a breed of sheep
the highest summit of the hills on the English-Scottish border

explanation.surface: Cloth at the upper end of a product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of the range' sounds like the best goods but is a mountain peak, the summit of the Cheviot Hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweed woven from sheep's wool, and the highest hill of the range on the border with Scotland.

clue.text: So upset after: blunder in examination

indicators.note: after puts the turned word behind the blunder in the answer

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or blunder

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word So is turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed after making a mistake in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS. A Tripos is the Cambridge honours degree exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the final honours examination at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Each one is in peace movement

indicators.note: is in tells us the letter for one sits inside the rearranged letters
movement means the letters of peace are moved around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Every single person belongs to a pacifist campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' turns PEACE into APECE; 'is in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in costing a pound apiece.

clue.text: He forgives Palmer en route for Canterbury

definitions.meaning: one who excuses or absolves an offence
a palmer is a pilgrim, and one of Chaucer's pilgrims travelling to Canterbury sells indulgences

explanation.surface: A golfer named Palmer, driving to Canterbury, lets someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palmer' looks like a surname but is an old word for a pilgrim; Chaucer's Canterbury Tales has such a pilgrim among its characters.
explanation.definitionFit: One who grants forgiveness, and the indulgence-seller among Chaucer's pilgrims in the Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Light and flimsy as, perhaps, some grass when just cut

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged some other way
just cut means the word grass is trimmed by its final letter

explanation.surface: Something delicate, like freshly mown grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just cut' trims GRASS to GRAS; 'perhaps' rearranges SOME plus GRAS. 'as' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is spider silk, and by extension anything delicate and insubstantial.

clue.text: Pass order to hairdresser?

definitions.meaning: a pass is a document authorising entry
a customer telling a stylist to give their hair a curling treatment

explanation.surface: A request made at the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into PERM IT, an instruction to curl the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is a licence allowing entry, and a hair-curling instruction read as two words.

clue.text: Songs Hitler heard?

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: Hitler was der Fuhrer, German for the leader

explanation.surface: Asking whether the dictator listened to music.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuhrer means leader, and LEADER sounds like LIEDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Toy broken in half by Jew in Californian park

indicators.note: broken in half means only one half of the toy word is kept

parts.note: a yo-yo is a toy spun on a string
a Jew is a Semite

explanation.surface: A child's plaything snapped by someone in a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken in half' cuts YOYO to YO.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a national park in the Sierra Nevada, famous for granite cliffs and waterfalls.
